reviews.title: Calculatingly Addictive
reviews.text: Truly careful thought went into this game, and it’s the very most successfully manipulative I’ve seen. I mean this as a compliment. The game is deeply addictive no matter how good you think you are at avoiding that, thanks surely to some very skilled psychologists and mathematicians working on this. Ads aren’t forced in your face, micro-transactions feel really worth it, and each new level or mini-game comes at just the right time to keep you entirely hooked. It’s literally just a game where you try to get lots of eggs, but boy is it impressively designed. You should always try to be aware of manipulation, but if you understand what this game can do to your brain, then it’s a very efficient way to get them happy chemicals flowing. reviews.title: Almost perfect
reviews.text: I love this game. That being said, there was one update that has made it nearly unplayable. It used to be that you could work on contract farms offline, I don’t know why this has changed but I can’t anymore, being someone who does not have constant access to WiFi, this has made it very difficult for me to do anything because, if I don’t switch to my main farm while online, it will just sit there with the syncing screen until I do get online. Also, if I am away from my contract farm for more that a handful of hours, like when I am working, it appears that there is too much data for the game to handle and it gets stuck on the syncing page. I can’t switch farms, make chickens, or even get to the help section. If this where fixed to play offline again and also not freeze when you try to update your contracts that would make this a five star game for me.

reviews.title: Best Idle Game!
reviews.text:
I initially downloaded this because I thought the chickens running were kinda cute and funny. I expected it to be your standard idle game, where you do the same thing for the entire time and get minor increases to things with no other content. But this game, despite the main gameplay still being holding down a button, actually adds some cool descriptions and funny newspaper ads about recent "events" and advances in eggs. (I wouldn't go so far as to call it "lore", but it's still pretty entertaining). 
It also doesn't take ages to advance. Sure it takes slightly longer, but epic research makes sure you always go further with each farm you make. Also, the ads are ONLY for rewards at your own decision, not a random occurrence that messes up your thought process. 
TLDR: it's a good game

reviews.title: Great Game; Bad Algorithm
reviews.text: I love this game. It’s so simple but somehow stays entertaining for months and years. The only thing I really hate about it is that the auto-join algorithm for co-ops is clearly designed to give you co-ops with lower member numbers, which is fine for smaller contracts, but if the contract has a maximum of 20+ players per co-op, you can basically forget about actually finishing, because once your co-op hits 8-10 players, it stops being shown to new ones, so no one else joins and it’s impossible to meet the goals. The current 50-member co-op contract is a joke; most scrape up less than 10 players before vanishing from the options, leaving them doomed to failure as nobody else joins and the co-op never fills (or even gets close to filling!) and can’t produce enough to fulfill the contract. Devs really need to fix this issue; it’s no fun to play when you’re guaranteed to lose.

reviews.title: Lots and Lots of Chickens
reviews.text:
I don’t think I’ve ever really played an idle game before Egg, Inc., so I don’t have any experience with the genre. But in a category called “Idle Clicker”, experience isn’t something you really need. At least, not for Egg, Inc.. I was able to get into it easily from the get-go. 
   The one flaw this game has becomes evident once you reach the Tachyon egg. You have to spend a lot of time clicking the Hatchery button and upgrading things one at a time for even a fraction of progress, so it doesn’t really feel like you accomplish anything until you’re magically ready to upgrade to the next egg, which will be even worse. At the time I’m writing this, I’m a third through the Dilithium egg, so I’ve not finished the game. Maybe this becomes less of an issue later on, but I don’t think it should be an issue at all.
   Great game, would recommend.

reviews.title: This game is surprisingly FUN!
reviews.text: First things first, this game is very fun. Like the top review says, it is a great idle game. I’ve spent endless hours tapping away and holding down the chicken release button to earn as much money as possible. I’ve made it a personal goal of mine to unlock every single egg type in the game. My only gripe would have to be about the screen perspective of the app. I can barely see anything on my screen (IPhone 11) and I wish there was a zoom out feature or an ability to turn the orientation of perspective. I know there is a “farm-to-table” mode which works so much better than the “default” positioning, but can that be added to the game without having to go farm to table? When I’m laying in bed playing this, I don’t want to have to get up just to make my in-game viewpoint more practical to use. Other than this gripe I would rate it a 5. With the perspective, I knocked it down a star
